messages:
nina: Hit a weird one during local testing. I have a global `/etc/redwood/profiles.yaml` supplied by infra and a `~/.config/redwood/profiles.yaml` from my devbox. Running `redwoodctl local-run` picks the wrong API key for the 'staging' profile—it's using the system one instead of my user override. Anyone know the precedence rules?

carlos: We intended user config to override system, but I recall we merged by filename then by last-modified time which is brittle. If both files define a profile with the same name we should prefer `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/redwood` first.

nina: Confirmed: `/etc/redwood` has `staging` with a generic key; my `~/.config/redwood` has `staging` with my personal dev key. `redwoodctl local-run --profile staging` still uses the system key. That blocks debugging.

priya: Oof. Two problems here: (1) merge strategy and (2) lack of visibility for users to see which source won. Suggestion: add `redwoodctl profiles inspect staging` that prints the effective profile plus source path and last-modified timestamps. That should make debugging easy.

carlos: I can repro locally. Current code loads a list of paths: `/etc/redwood/profiles.yaml`, `$SNAP_USER_DATA/.config/redwood/profiles.yaml` (if snap), and `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/redwood/profiles.yaml` and merges them in the order returned by glob, which was non-deterministic.

nina: Repro steps I used:```bash
# system file
sudo tee /etc/redwood/profiles.yaml <<'YAML'
profiles:
  staging:
    api_key: sys-XXXX
YAML

# user file
mkdir -p ~/.config/redwood
tee ~/.config/redwood/profiles.yaml <<'YAML'
profiles:
  staging:
    api_key: user-YYYY
YAML

redwoodctl local-run --profile staging
# observed: used sys-XXXX
```

priya: Good repro. For immediate mitigation, you can explicitly pass `--config /home/nina/.config/redwood/profiles.yaml` to force user config, but we should fix merge precedence.

eng-platform: Heads upwe ship `/etc/redwood` in some images to provide a default profile. Fixing precedence may change behavior for some customers; we should add a migration note and keep the old behavior behind an opt-in flag for one release cycle.

carlos: Plan: (A) change merge order to prefer XDG/user over system, (B) add `redwoodctl profiles inspect` and `--config`/`REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR` env var if users want to override, (C) add a warning message in `local-run` when a profile name is shadowed by multiple sources, listing the chosen source.

priya: Also recommend adding a small diagnostic command `redwoodctl profiles list --sources` that prints all profiles and where they came from. Low-risk UX win.

nina: I'm happy to test changes. Also, for the docs quickstart we should add a note about `/etc` defaults and how `--config` or `REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR` can be used for dev overrides.

dx-bot: NOTE: Created GH issue #712 (devex: profiles merge precedence and diagnostics). Assigned to @carlos.

eng-platform: We'll coordinate a compatibility notice and add an integration test to ensure awkward merges are caught. Also adding a unit test that simulates `/etc` + `~/.config` with conflicting profile names.

nina: Thanks all. For the immediate blocker, `redwoodctl local-run --config ~/.config/redwood/profiles.yaml` worked for me.
thread_text: I have a global /etc/redwood/profiles.yaml and a user ~/.config/redwood/profiles.yaml. local-run picks the system profile instead of my user override; what's the precedence?
